body:
### Problem

Executing operator with a custom textobject triggers different `CmdAtom` events compared to the equivalent built-in application. In particular, the type is `mapping` and not `operator`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the following `init.lua`:

    ```lua
    -- Custom textobject that act the same as `$`
    local textobject = function() vim.cmd('normal! v$') end
    vim.keymap.set('o', 'gt', textobject, {})

    -- Prepare buffer text for repro
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, { 'aaa', 'bbb' })
    vim.bo.modified = false

    -- Track all `CmdAtom` events
    _G.cmdatom_log = {}
    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('CmdAtom', { callback = function(ev) table.insert(_G.cmdatom_log, ev.data) end })
    ```

2. `nvim --clean -u init.lua`
3. Do one of the following:
    3.1. Type `d`-`gt`. Executing `:=cmdatom_log` shows the following entries:

        ```lua
        { {
          changed = true,
          lhs = "dgt",
          moved = false,
          pos = { 1, 0 },
          type = "mapping",
          undoseq = 2
        } }
        ```

    3.2. Type `d`-`$`. Executing `:=cmdatom_log` shows the following entries:

        ```lua
        { {
          changed = true,
          cmd = "$",
          keys = "d$",
          lhs = "d$",
          moved = false,
          operator = "d",
          pos = { 1, 0 },
          type = "operator",
          undoseq = 2
        } }
        ```

### Expected behavior

Executing an operator always results (at least) in a `CmdAtom` event that shows that the operator was applied.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1410+g510f61555b

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

No, doesn't have this functionality

### Operating system/version

 EndeavourOS Linux x86_64, 7.1.9-arch1-2

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

### Installation

Appimage

comment_data.body:
The reason this is relevant is because the built-in `.` always repeats the last `g@` application *regardless of whether it resulted in edit or not*. This behavior is really useful when implementing custom operators that are worth being dot-repeatable.

So in order to capture this in `CmdAtom` based `.`, there has to be a check for `ev.data.operator == 'g@'` (whether to include this behavior in `:h edit-repeat` is another question). Which currently only works with built-in textobjects and not custom ones.

To test this, add to the above `init.lua` the following custom operator implementation:

```lua
-- Custom operator that doesn't actually edit text
_G.log = {}
local operator = function()
  vim.o.operatorfunc = function(...) table.insert(_G.log, { ... }) end
  return 'g@'
end
vim.keymap.set('n', 'gh', operator, { expr = true })
```

Typing `gh`-`gt`-`.` results in `_G.log = { { 'char' }, { 'char' } }`, i.e. it is dot-repeated even there is no edit.

However, if the `.` comes from `:h edit-repeat`, this is not dot-repeatable. Primarily because there is no text edit, but also because it is not captured as `g@` operator application. Here is the output of `cmdatom_log` after `gh`-`gt`:

```lua
{ {
    changed = false,
    lhs = "gh",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "mapping",
    undoseq = 1
  }, {
    changed = false,
    lhs = "g@gt",
    moved = false,
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "mapping",
    undoseq = 1
  } }
```

Compared to `gh`-`$`:

```lua
{ {
    changed = false,
    cmd = "$",
    keys = "g@$",
    lhs = "gh$",
    moved = false,
    operator = "g@",
    pos = { 1, 0 },
    type = "operator",
    undoseq = 1
  } }
```

title: CmdAtom: executing operator with custom textobject doesn't result in `CmdAtom.type='operator'`
